title: GDE 1: Admissions in Gauteng
description: How Grade 1 and Grade 8 admissions work in Gauteng public schools: the regulations, the online system, feeder zones, placement order, documents, waiting lists and appeals.

lessons.title: The Gauteng admission rules
lessons.summary: Which regulations apply, who decides, and what changes every year.
lessons.body:
## 🏛️ Gauteng has its own admission rules

The South African Schools Act 84 of 1996 (SASA) sets the national framework for admissions in section 5, as amended by the Basic Education Laws Amendment Act 32 of 2024 (BELA Act). On top of that, Gauteng has its own provincial regulations. This module applies to Gauteng public ordinary schools only, not independent schools.

The Gauteng rules are the **Regulations Relating to the Admission of Learners to Public Schools**, published as General Notice 4138 of 13 July 2001 in Provincial Gazette No. 129. They were made by the MEC for Education under section 11(1) of the Gauteng School Education Act 6 of 1995. They have been amended twice:

1. **General Notice 1160 of 2012**, in force from 9 May 2012. This was the version challenged in the Constitutional Court.
2. **Provincial Notice 268 of 2019**, which rewrote large parts, including feeder zones, the placement order and the 30 kilometre categories.

Regulation 19 (inserted in 2019) gives the short title as the Regulations Relating to the Admission of Learners at Public Schools, 2001.

> ⚠️ Watch out: regulation numbers differ between copies of these regulations, because the 2019 amendment renumbered parts of the text. This course uses the numbering in the consolidated text that shows both amendments. Quote the title and the topic, not only a number, when you write to the district.

## 🧭 Who decides what

Regulation 2 makes the Head of Department (HOD) responsible for administering admissions. Regulation 2A(2)(b) says the HOD has the final authority to admit a learner to a school. SASA section 5, as amended by the BELA Act, also gives the HOD the final say on admission.

The SGB still matters. Under regulation 2B the SGB determines the school's admission policy, but:

- the policy only takes effect once the HOD approves it (regulation 2B(4))
- the SGB must review it every three years, when circumstances require, or when the HOD asks (regulation 2B(8))
- if the policy conflicts with the regulations, the regulations win (regulation 17)

## 🚫 What a school may not do

Regulation 2A(1) lists grounds on which a learner may not be refused, including unfair discrimination, a parent who cannot or has not paid fees, a parent who will not sign the mission statement or code of conduct, or a parent who refuses to sign a waiver of claims. A learner may also not be refused because the parent cannot produce the documents.

Two more rules catch schools out:

- **No confidential reports.** Regulation 2A(3) bars the SGB or staff from asking the learner's current school or parent for a report on finances, fee affordability, employment, health or behaviour that could be used to discriminate.
- **No admission tests.** Regulation 2C(1) bars the SGB from setting any admission test. Only a focus school (for example a sport or arts school) may test, and then only with the HOD's prior written approval (regulation 2C(2) and (3)).

## 📅 What changes every year

The regulations stay fairly stable, but the **dates, phases, the number of schools a parent may choose and the way documents are submitted** are set fresh each year. Regulation 5(1) requires the HOD to publish the application and admission period every year during the second term.

At national level, the Minister published draft Admission of Learners to Public Schools Regulations under SASA in August 2025 for comment. At the time of writing we could not confirm that a final version has been gazetted. If it has, national rules may override parts of the Gauteng regulations.

> 💡 Tip: every year, ask the district for the current GDE admissions circular and keep it with your admission policy. Treat it as the source for dates and process.

## ✅ Key points
- Gauteng admissions follow GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019.
- The HOD has the final authority to admit a learner (regulation 2A(2)(b) and SASA s5 as amended by BELA).
- The SGB's admission policy needs HOD approval and must yield to the regulations (regulations 2B and 17).
- No admission tests and no confidential reports, except approved tests at focus schools.
- Dates and process details change every year: check the current GDE circular.

lessons.title: Applying online and the yearly cycle
lessons.summary: The online system, the steps and deadlines, full schools and late applications.
lessons.body:
## 💻 Grade 1 and Grade 8 apply online

Regulation 5(2) of the Gauteng admission regulations says an application for an entry grade learner may only be made through the online system on the GDE website. The regulations define entry grade learners as learners going into Grade 1 or Grade 8, or the lowest grade of a school that starts at another grade (excluding Grade R).

For learners going into other grades, parents apply directly to the school. Regulation 11 covers transfers between schools, with a transfer form, the transfer card and the latest report.

> ⚠️ Watch out: a child in Grade R at your school has no automatic place in your Grade 1. Regulation 10(2) says a Grade R learner is not entitled to be re-enrolled the next year unless he or she qualifies under the regulations. Parents must still apply online.

## 🗓️ The yearly cycle

The regulations set the steps. The GDE circular sets the dates.

1. **Dates published.** The HOD publishes the application and admission period each year during the second term (regulation 5(1)).
2. **Parents apply online** during the application period.
3. **Documents.** Regulation 6(1) requires documents to reach the school within seven school days of the end of the application period. In practice the GDE circular says how and when to submit them, so follow the circular for that year.
4. **Waiting lists.** After a complete application, the HOD places the learner on a waiting list, sends the list to the school and tells the parent which list the learner is on (regulation 5(3)).
5. **Outcomes.** Within 21 school days after the application period ends, the HOD must tell applicants whether they were successful (regulation 5(4)(a)).
6. **Accept the offer.** Successful parents must confirm acceptance within seven school days of being told (regulation 5(4)(b)).
7. **Reasons and rights.** Unsuccessful parents must get written reasons within 14 school days and be told of their right to object and appeal (regulation 5(4)(c) and (d)).
8. **Unplaced learners.** If a learner is still unplaced 30 school days after the admission period ends, the HOD may place the learner at any school that has not been declared full and has no unplaced learners left on its waiting list (regulation 5(5)).

### 📌 Example: the 2027 intake

For learners starting school in 2027, the GDE window opened on 5 August 2026 and closed on 4 September 2026, according to GDE announcements reported in the media. These dates are only for that one cycle. The window has moved between years, so never reuse old dates in a newsletter to parents.

## 🏫 Full schools and late applicants

Under regulation 8, the HOD decides each school's objective entry level enrolment capacity and may declare a school full, on the HOD's own initiative or at the school's request. A school that reaches that capacity must be declared full and is told in writing.

To help with this, regulation 4A requires the principal to send the HOD capacity information by 30 June each year: classrooms and their condition, how classrooms are allocated to grades, the curriculum and staffing. The HOD must reply with the capacity determination by 30 September.

Parents who miss the application period lose any preferential right at full schools. Regulation 7(5) says such learners may be placed where there is space.

> 💡 Tip: put the 30 June capacity return in your SGB year planner. A school that sends accurate figures is in a far stronger position when the district asks it to take more learners.

## 👨‍👩‍👧 What the SGB can tell parents

- Apply online, in the window, even if an older child is at the school.
- Keep the application reference and any SMS from the system.
- Accept an offer within the deadline or it may be lost.
- Schools do not choose who gets placed. The GDE places learners using the order in the regulations.

## ✅ Key points
- Grade 1 and Grade 8 applications in Gauteng are online only (regulation 5(2)); other grades apply to the school.
- Grade R learners are not guaranteed a Grade 1 place at the same school (regulation 10(2)).
- Offers must be accepted within seven school days (regulation 5(4)(b)).
- Principals send capacity information by 30 June each year (regulation 4A).
- Exact dates change every year: check the current GDE circular.

lessons.title: Feeder zones and the placement order
lessons.summary: What a feeder zone is, how the courts shaped it, and who gets placed first.
lessons.body:
## 🗺️ What a feeder zone is

The Gauteng admission regulations define a feeder zone as the area from which a school accepts its core intake. Under regulation 4(1), the HOD, not the SGB, determines feeder zones by notice in the Provincial Gazette. Focus schools and schools for learners with special education needs are excluded (regulation 4(2)).

When setting a feeder zone, regulation 4(3) requires the HOD to consider school capacity, the language and curricula of nearby schools, population and enrolment projections, and the need for geographical and spatial transformation. Before deciding, the HOD must publish proposed zones, give SGBs and parents 30 days for written representations and seriously consider them (regulation 4(5)).

## ⚖️ How the courts shaped this

In 2016 the Constitutional Court heard a challenge by the Federation of Governing Bodies for South African Schools (FEDSAS) to the 2012 Gauteng amendments. The court upheld the MEC's power to make these regulations and confirmed that the provincial department, not each SGB, has the final say on admissions in the public system. It treated the old default feeder zones (based on distance or a parent's work address) as transitional and ordered the MEC to determine proper feeder zones. After an extension, the GDE published feeder zones in November 2018, reported as widening the zone to a 30 kilometre radius. FEDSAS criticised the process.

The 2019 amendment (PN 268 of 2019) then rewrote the placement rules around feeder zones and a 30 km radius.

> ⚠️ Watch out: media reports said the 2018 determination gave every school a 30 km feeder zone, while the 2019 regulations list "within the feeder zone" and "within 30 km" as separate categories. We could not confirm the current official feeder zone map for each school. Ask your district which determination applies to your school before you tell a parent they are inside or outside the zone.

## 🥇 The order of placement

Regulation 7(2) sets the categories, and regulation 7(3) says applications are ranked in this order and then by the date the application was received:

1. **Home closest to the school within the feeder zone.**
2. **A sibling attending the school.**
3. **A parent's place of work within the feeder zone.**
4. **Home within a 30 kilometre radius of the school.**
5. **Home beyond a 30 kilometre radius of the school.**

Categories 1 to 4 go onto **waiting list A**. Learners who do not qualify for list A (category 5) go onto **waiting list B** (regulation 7(4)).

### 👧 Who counts as a sibling

The regulations define a sibling as a learner who is enrolled at the school in the year the applicant wants to start, lives in the same household, and shares at least one parent with the applicant. A cousin who lives with the family does not qualify, and nor does a brother who has just finished matric. The GDE system also limits which grades of the sibling count each year, so check the current circular.

## 🏫 Boarding schools and special cases

Regulation 5(7) lets the HOD, on application by a school with boarding, allow a fixed number of boarders who would not otherwise qualify. Regulation 9 requires an ordinary public school to admit a learner with special education needs unless the procedures in the Gauteng School Education Act show that a special school is needed.

> 💡 Tip: when a parent asks "why did a family further away get in?", the answer is usually a sibling or a work address in the feeder zone, or an earlier application date. Point them to regulation 7 and their right to object.

## ✅ Key points
- The HOD determines feeder zones by notice in the Provincial Gazette (regulation 4).
- An SGB or parent may appeal a feeder zone determination to the MEC within 30 days; the MEC decides within 30 days (regulation 4B).
- Placement order: feeder zone home, sibling, parent's work in feeder zone, within 30 km, beyond 30 km (regulation 7(2)).
- Ties are broken by application date (regulation 7(3)); list A covers categories 1 to 4, list B the rest.
- Confirm your school's current feeder zone with the district.

lessons.title: Documents, waiting lists and appeals
lessons.summary: What parents must provide, how waiting lists work, and how to object and appeal to the MEC.
lessons.body:
## 📄 Documents parents need

Regulation 6(1) of the Gauteng admission regulations lists the documents for an entry grade application:

- a certified copy of the child's birth certificate
- a certified copy of the parent's ID, or a sworn affidavit if the parent has none
- proof of the parent's residential or work address
- where the applicant is not the natural parent, documents showing the legal relationship with the child
- for primary schools, proof of immunisation from a public or registered private health facility
- the transfer card and latest school report, if the child is at another school
- proof of the sibling relationship, if the parent relies on a sibling

Regulation 6(2) says **no other documents may be requested**. A school that asks for payslips, bank statements or a behaviour report is breaking the rules (see also regulation 2A(3)).

### 🧾 When documents are missing

A child is not turned away for lack of documents (regulation 2A(1)(e)). Under regulation 6(3) the application is accepted provisionally, and the principal must tell the parent where to get the documents. The parent must show within two weeks that they have applied for them. Under regulation 6(4) the provisional application lapses if they do not, or if the documents are not in within six weeks, although the District Director may extend this for good cause.

Principals must report undocumented learners each year through the District Director and keep a database of them (regulation 6(5)). Regulation 12 covers non-citizens, including study visas and proof of an application to Home Affairs. SASA section 5, as amended by the BELA Act, also protects undocumented learners: check the current circular on how the GDE applies it.

> ⚠️ Watch out: the way documents are submitted (uploaded online or taken to a school) and the deadline are set in each year's GDE circular. Do not rely on last year's instructions.

## ⏳ Waiting lists

Every applicant goes onto waiting list A or B (regulation 7(4)). Regulation 15(5) says that, after the admission period, the Department must tell a parent on request where their child is on the school's waiting lists. A learner may still be placed from a waiting list when other parents decline offers or fail to accept in time.

## 🙋 Objections and appeals to the MEC

Gauteng uses two steps, set out in regulation 16:

1. **Objection to the HOD.** Within **seven school days** of receiving the written reasons for refusal (regulation 5(4)(c) and (d)), the parent may object to the HOD, using a form like Annexure D. It is sent care of the District Director.
2. **Appeal to the MEC.** If still unhappy, the parent may appeal to the MEC within **seven school days** of being told the HOD's decision or reasons, using a form like Annexure E (regulation 16(4)).
3. **MEC decision.** The MEC must decide within **15 school days** of receiving the appeal and give reasons if the appeal is not upheld (regulation 16(5)).

This matches the national right in SASA section 5(9): a learner or parent who is refused admission may appeal to the MEC.

Regulation 16(1) requires the principal to tell a refused parent in writing about these rights.

### 💬 Example

A mother is told her son did not get a Grade 8 place. She lives 4 km away but the school says she is outside its feeder zone. She asks the school for the written reasons, objects to the HOD within seven school days, and attaches her proof of address and waiting list number. If the HOD says no, she appeals to the MEC within seven school days of that answer.

> 💡 Tip: the SGB should not argue a placement dispute with a parent. Give the parent the written reasons and the objection route, and keep a copy.

## ✅ Key points
- Only the documents in regulation 6(1) may be asked for (regulation 6(2)).
- Missing documents lead to a provisional application, not a refusal (regulations 2A(1)(e) and 6(3)).
- Object to the HOD within seven school days, then appeal to the MEC within seven school days (regulation 16).
- The MEC must decide within 15 school days (regulation 16(5)); SASA s5(9) gives the national right of appeal.
- Check the current GDE circular for how documents are submitted each year.

questions.text: What are the Gauteng regulations that govern admissions to public schools?

options.text: The Regulations Relating to the Admission of Learners to Public Schools, GN 4138 of 2001, as amended in 2012 and 2019
The Gauteng Admissions Act of 2019
The National Admission Policy for Ordinary Public Schools of 1998, with no provincial rules
Each school's own admission policy, approved by the SGB alone

questions.explanation: The Gauteng rules are GN 4138 of 13 July 2001, made under s11(1) of the Gauteng School Education Act 6 of 1995 and amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019.

questions.text: Who has the final authority to admit a learner to a Gauteng public school?

options.text: The principal
The SGB chairperson
The Head of Department
The parent body at a general meeting

questions.explanation: Regulation 2A(2)(b) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) gives the HOD the final authority, consistent with SASA s5 as amended by the BELA Act.

questions.text: May an SGB in Gauteng ask a learner's current school for a report on the learner's behaviour before admitting the learner?

options.text: Yes, if the parent agrees
Yes, but only for Grade 8
No, regulation 2A(3) forbids requesting such a confidential report
Only if the school is declared full

questions.explanation: Regulation 2A(3) and (4) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) bar the SGB or staff from requesting a confidential report on finances, health, misconduct or behaviour.

questions.text: How must a parent apply for a Grade 1 place at a Gauteng public school?

options.text: On paper at the school office
Through the GDE online application system
By email to the district office
By letter to the MEC

questions.explanation: Regulation 5(2) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) says entry grade applications may only be made through the online system on the Department's website.

questions.text: A child is in Grade R at your primary school. What is the position for Grade 1?

options.text: The child is automatically re-enrolled into Grade 1
The child gets first priority above all others
The child must still apply, as a Grade R learner is not entitled to re-enrolment unless otherwise eligible
The child may only apply to a different school

questions.explanation: Regulation 10(2) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) says a Grade R learner is not entitled to be re-enrolled the next year unless otherwise entitled to admission under the regulations.

questions.text: Who determines a Gauteng school's feeder zone?

options.text: The SGB in its admission policy
The Head of Department, by notice in the Provincial Gazette
The ward councillor
The principal, each year

questions.explanation: Regulation 4(1) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) requires the HOD to determine feeder zones by notice in the Provincial Gazette, after consultation under regulation 4(5).

questions.text: Which applicant ranks highest in the Gauteng placement order?

options.text: A learner whose home is within 30 km of the school
A learner whose parent works within the feeder zone
A learner with a sibling at the school
A learner whose home is closest to the school within the feeder zone

questions.explanation: Regulation 7(2)(a) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) puts residence closest to the school within the feeder zone first, followed by sibling, parent's work in the feeder zone, within 30 km and beyond 30 km.

questions.text: Which of these documents may a school NOT ask for in a Gauteng entry grade application?

options.text: The parent's latest payslip
A certified copy of the birth certificate
Proof of residential or work address
Proof of immunisation for a primary school

questions.explanation: Regulation 6(2) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) says no documents other than those in regulation 6(1) may be requested. A payslip is not on the list.

questions.text: A parent cannot produce the child's birth certificate. What happens?

options.text: The application is rejected
The application is accepted provisionally while the parent obtains the documents
The child is placed on waiting list B automatically
The SGB decides at its next meeting

questions.explanation: Regulations 2A(1)(e) and 6(3) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) say a learner may not be refused for lack of documents; the application is accepted provisionally and the parent must show within two weeks that the documents were applied for.

questions.text: A parent's objection to the HOD is turned down. Within what period may the parent appeal to the MEC?

options.text: 30 days
Seven school days
14 calendar days
Three months

questions.explanation: Regulation 16(4) of the Gauteng admission regulations (GN 4138 of 2001, as amended by GN 1160 of 2012 and PN 268 of 2019) allows an appeal to the MEC within 7 school days; the MEC must decide within 15 school days (regulation 16(5)). SASA s5(9) gives the national right of appeal.
